claim_support.claim: The incident involves a missed detection of sustained ventricular fibrillation (VF), which is a safety-critical event with high potential for serious harm or death if not flagged in real-time.
Although the specific episode self-resolved and no adverse outcome was recorded, the failure to flag VF represents a critical degradation in a life-saving function.
The missing confidence-score log prevents full root cause analysis of why the algorithm failed on this specific data pattern.

Under 21 CFR § 820.10(c) (Design Controls), manufacturers must ensure design and development processes validate that devices perform as intended; a missed VF episode suggests a potential gap in validation coverage or an unaddressed edge case.
EU MDR Article 83 requires the post-market surveillance system to actively gather data on safety performance and determine corrective actions when such events occur.
The severity is elevated (Severity 3) because it involves a failure of a primary safety function with serious potential harm, even though no injury occurred in this specific instance.
